subject: Deployment pathing and dedicated sizing follow-ups
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Subject: Deployment pathing and dedicated sizing follow-ups

Hi Avery / Samir —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and the open items we promised to follow up on related to deployment mode and dedicated sizing so we can lock a proposed configuration for procurement: 

What we heard on the call: 
- You prefer starting on Dedicated capacity (predictable SLOs, committed throughput) with a plan to evaluate Private VPC for the 2027 compliance milestone.
- Primary workload: high-concurrency chat/completion API for user-facing product search assistants (real-time responses).
- Current baseline: light production traffic today; target go-live baseline is modest but peak events create 10x spikes.

Open items we need from you to finalize a sizing proposal: 
1) Target sustained requests/sec (typical) and peak requests/sec (burst).
2) Average and peak token footprint (input + output) per request and % of long-tail requests (>1024 tokens).
3) Desired p95 latency SLO and whether strict p50/p95 latency SLAs are required.
4) Any hard constraints on GPU type (H100 vs A100) or must we optimize for cost?
5) Region preference and data residency needs.

What we’ll deliver after we have those answers: a Dedicated SKU mix (GPU flavors + count), expected concurrent request capacity, estimated token/sec throughput, and a cost ballpark plus autoscaling recommendations. 

Attachment: quantifyai-dedicated-worksheet-v1.xlsx — simple worksheet we’ll use to fill your numbers and produce a sizing snapshot.

Proposed next steps: 
- If you can reply with the items above, we’ll produce a 1-page recommended config within 48 hours.
- Recommend a 30-min follow-up Thursday to review the worksheet together.

Thanks —

From: Avery Grant <avery@quantifyai.com>

Subject: Re: Deployment pathing and dedicated sizing follow-ups

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. Answers below to the questionnaire so you can run numbers: 

1) Traffic profile
- Typical steady-state: ~12 requests/sec (RPS) across our cluster.
- Peak (marketing events): short bursts up to ~90 RPS for <10 minutes.
- Expected growth: 2–3x over the next 6 months.

2) Token footprint
- Typical request (user prompt + model output): ~350 tokens total.
- 80% of requests are <= 512 tokens; 15% fall between 512–1024; 5% are long-tail (~1500–2048 tokens).

3) Latency SLO
- Desired p95 generation latency: <= 350ms. P50 target: <= 120ms. If we can get p95 <= 200ms that’s ideal but we understand cost tradeoffs.

4) GPU preference / constraints
- No hard requirement to H100; cost matters. If you can present a mixed-pool option (a couple of H100 for low-latency frontends + A100s for cost-efficient capacity), that would be perfect.

5) Region / compliance
- US West (primary) for low latency to our user base.
- We’ll want to evaluate Private VPC before signing a 12-month committed plan, but Dedicated in US West is fine to start.

Procurement note: loop in procurement (cc’ing Samir). We’ll review the config and budget, then propose a decision timeline next week.

Thanks —

Avery Grant
Head of Product, QuantifyAI
avery@quantifyai.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 13:31:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Deployment pathing and dedicated sizing follow-ups (internal sizing draft)

Internal draft based on Avery's numbers — quick notes / recommended config to propose: 

Design goals: meet p95 <= 350ms for 80% of traffic, handle 90 RPS short bursts, support growth to 36 RPS sustained.

Recommended starting mix (US West):
- Frontend latency pool: 2 x H100 80GB (low-latency nodes, pinned for real-time requests).
- Bulk capacity pool: 3 x A100 80GB (cost-efficient for steady-state and queue-able bursts).
- Autoscaling: keep a 20% warm buffer and allow burst scaling with up to 2 additional A100 nodes on demand.

Estimated capacity (ballpark):
- With this mix, expected sustained capacity ~35 RPS at ~350 tokens/request with p95 ~300–400ms depending on concurrency and batching settings.
- Peak 90 RPS for 10 minutes: with autoscale to +2 A100s and frontend H100s, p95 expected to remain <500ms (some queueing).

Configuration/ops notes:
- Suggest enabling prefix KV caching where possible for repeated prompts (saves tokens).
- Recommend quantization experimentation (INT8) on A100 pool for cost savings; validate for quality.
- Provide two SKU options in proposal: "Latency-first" (3x H100) and "Balanced" (2x H100 + 4x A100).

I attached a quick worksheet (quantifyai-dedicated-worksheet-v1.xlsx) with rough calc — we should populate with Avery's final expected growth and token numbers before sending external.

Ben — can you run a quick cost delta (monthly committed) between the Balanced and Latency-first SKUs so Jordan can present a clean choice?

-Marissa
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Avery / Samir — thanks for the fast reply and the clear numbers. We’ll turn this into a concise proposal. Quick summary of what we’ll send within 48 hours: 

1) Two recommended Dedicated SKU options (one latency-first, one balanced cost/perf) with:
   - GPU mix and counts
   - Expected sustained and peak RPS capacity at your stated token mix
   - Expected p95 latency ranges and where risk of queueing occurs
   - Monthly committed cost (ballpark) and incremental cost to add burst nodes

2) Operational notes: autoscaling policy, caching suggestions, quantization caveats, and a migration path to Private VPC when you’re ready.

Proposed next meeting: Thu 26 Nov, 10:00am PT — 30 minutes to review the worksheet and pick a SKU. Are you available? If not, suggest two alternatives.

Action items for QuantifyAI: confirm acceptance of the baseline numbers (12 RPS steady / 90 RPS peak; token mix as listed) or send any corrections.

Action items for Redwood: Marissa + Ben to complete the worksheet and cost delta; Jordan to schedule the review and circulate the one-pager.

Thanks — talk soon.
